page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the cost-efficient E2 instance family. It features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage for boot and data volumes.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear tradeoff between raw computational speed and memory capacity. The server exhibits weak CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core metrics falling into the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores rank in the bottom 10%, reflecting the lower-frequency Intel Xeon processor. However, the system maintains a stable memory subsystem, achieving an average rating in Passmark memory benchmarks, though uncached large-block memory read and write speeds remain in the lower 25% tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-highmem-4 offers a dense memory allocation without the premium cost associated with high-performance compute cores. This makes it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU throughput. Recommended workloads include small-scale databases, caching layers, light enterprise applications, and basic text generation tasks using small language models, where the 32 GB RAM buffer prevents out-of-memory errors during execution.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct tradeoff: while CPU-bound tasks like software compilation, ray tracing, and compression score in the bottom 10% to 25%, the memory subsystem achieves average marks in Passmark testing. This profile makes the instance a cost-efficient option for memory-heavy, low-CPU applications. It is best suited for small databases, caching systems, and light text generation tasks using small language models. The 32 GB memory capacity provides a stable buffer for memory-bound applications without the high cost of premium compute resources.
